distribution.title: Bernoulli distribution
distribution.intro: A Bernoulli random variable models one trial with success probability \(p\), where \(0\le p\le1\). It equals 1 for success and 0 for failure.
distribution.properties: The mean is \(p\) and the variance is \(p(1-p)\). The sum of \(n\) independent Bernoulli trials with common probability \(p\) has a binomial distribution.
distribution.course: The course uses Bernoulli samples to illustrate sufficient statistics, unbiased estimation, and hypothesis tests.
distribution.course_link: Find a sufficient statistic for Bernoulli trials
distribution.r_intro: These examples use functions from R’s stats package. For functions with d, p, q, and r prefixes, they compute a density or mass, cumulative probability, quantile, and random samples, respectively.
distribution.r_code:
dbinom(1, size = 1, prob = 0.3)
pbinom(0, size = 1, prob = 0.3)
qbinom(0.5, size = 1, prob = 0.3)
rbinom(100, size = 1, prob = 0.3)
